```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

What do observed prices and margins identify about coordinated pricing? This
example illustrates a **zero-supermarkup identification boundary**. It does not
claim a positive leadership markup or a full incentive-compatibility test when
timing is unidentified. Use **coordination 0.1.0** with compatible
**antitrust >= 0.99.43**. All inputs are illustrative; prices are currency per
unit and insideSize is inside quantity.

## Fit and inspect the boundary

Products 1–3 form a coalition; AB owns both products 1 and 2. Coalition membership
uses **product indices**, while ownership identifies firms. Product 4 is fringe.
At least one coalition and one fringe margin are needed by this constructor.

```{r ple-boundary}
library(antitrust)
library(coordination)
fit <- coordination::ple(
  prices = c(.93, .88, 1.10, 1.02),
  shares = c(.35, .25, .25, .15),
  margins = c(.40, NA, .35, .25),
  ownerPre = c("AB", "AB", "MC", "Fringe"),
  ownerPost = c("AB", "AB", "MC", "Fringe"),
  coalitionPre = 1:3, coalitionPost = 1:3, insideSize = 1000
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(product = fit@labels, observed_price = fit@prices,
  fitted_price = fit@pricePre), digits = 4)
list(supermarkup = fit@supermarkupPre,
     timing = fit@timingParam, binding_firm = fit@bindingFirm)
```

The equal-ownership warning is expected: this first scenario has no merger.
The fitted prices need not reproduce supplied prices exactly. Compare the two
price columns before applying this calibration to an empirical market.
The returned supermarkup is zero and the timing parameters and binding firm
are `NA`. Here the data identify no additional leadership supermarkup.
`NA` timing is absence of identification, not evidence that firms have zero
patience or that collusion is impossible.

```{r ple-boundary-check, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(abs(fit@supermarkupPre) < 1e-6,
          all(is.na(fit@timingParam)), is.na(fit@bindingFirm),
          all(is.finite(fit@pricePre)))
```

## Why zero slack is not a full IC result

With a valid timing parameter delta, the full firm slack compares leadership,
deviation and punishment profits:

\[
g_f=(\pi^{PL}_f-\pi^D_f)+\frac{\delta_f}{1-\delta_f}
(\pi^{PL}_f-\pi^B_f).
\]

The full incentive constraint is satisfied when this quantity is nonnegative.
When timing is missing, the method warns and returns only immediate payoff
differences. That truncated quantity cannot establish the repeated-game
condition above.

```{r immediate-payoffs}
calcSlack(fit)
```

The warning is part of the result's interpretation. Do not hide it and describe
the returned zeros as a successful sustainability test. Likewise, a nonmissing
binding-firm slot would require an explanation of the regime and identification
assumptions; it is not a probability that coordination occurs.

## Be explicit about pricing regimes

The public price method defaults to the `coordination` regime, whereas the
constructor solves its stored prices using `constrained`. Name the regime when
comparing reference prices.

```{r ple-regimes}
pricing_regimes <- data.frame(product = fit@labels,
  bertrand = antitrust::calcPrices(fit, preMerger = TRUE, regime = "bertrand"),
  coordination = antitrust::calcPrices(fit, preMerger = TRUE,
                                     regime = "coordination"),
  stored_constrained = fit@pricePre)
knitr::kable(pricing_regimes, digits = 4)
observed_minus_coordinated <- mean(fit@prices[1:3] -
                                    pricing_regimes$coordination[1:3])
```

Bertrand is the noncoordinated reference. Coordination uses the coalition's
coordinated-reference FOCs. The stored supermarkup is an **additional scalar
level-margin wedge over that coordinated reference**, not the entire
coordination-minus-Bertrand price difference. In this calibration the mean
observed-minus-coordinated price gap across coalition products is
`r sprintf("%.4f", observed_minus_coordinated)` currency/unit. That nonpositive
comparison is assigned the zero additional-wedge boundary, leaving timing
unidentified.

For example, product 1's Bertrand price is
`r sprintf("%.4f", pricing_regimes$bertrand[1])`, while its coordinated-reference
price is `r sprintf("%.4f", pricing_regimes$coordination[1])`, a
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * (pricing_regimes$coordination[1] / pricing_regimes$bertrand[1] - 1))`%
increase relative to Bertrand. Its stored constrained price equals the
coordinated reference here because the additional wedge is zero. Thus zero
additional supermarkup does not imply zero coordination-versus-Bertrand price
difference. The positive price gap is a regime comparison, not an identified
positive leadership wedge or an established repeated-game sustainability result.
These differences are not uncertainty intervals.

## What comes next

A positive leadership demonstration would require independently validated inputs
and a full timing/IC interpretation. Supplying a timing vector is a scenario
assumption, distinct from identifying timing from a binding constraint. This
guide deliberately makes no positive-coordination claim from the boundary case.

For an existing Bertrand fit and an explicit discount assumption, use
[Grim Trigger sustainability](grim-trigger.html) ([source](https://github.com/luciu5/coordination/blob/main/vignettes/grim-trigger.Rmd)). For sequential leadership or a
simultaneous strategic core, use [noncooperative role games](role-games.html) ([source](https://github.com/luciu5/coordination/blob/main/vignettes/role-games.Rmd));
those are different games from PLE. See `?ple`, `?calcSlack`, `?calcSupermarkup`
and the [model reference](https://github.com/luciu5/coordination/blob/main/doc/coordination-model-reference.md)
for longer identification notes and deterministic BLP integration. The economic
PLE framework follows Mansley, Miller, Sheu and Weinberg (2023), as cited in the
package help.
